This stays local — no data leaves your machine. Recommended for solo developers; skip if you work on multiple client codebases where cross-contamination would be a concern. Which do you prefer? <gstack-qid:cross-project-learnings>

options.label: Enable cross-project learnings (Recommended)

questions.question: Pass 7 surfaces one genuinely open product decision: what happens to the Export button during and after download? The plan currently specifies Export triggers a JSON download of saved preferences, but doesn't define the button state during the operation. How should Export behave? <gstack-qid:settings-export-state>

options.label: Fire-and-forget — no pending state (Recommended)
options.description: Browser handles the download dialog immediately. Export button stays enabled. No progress indicator needed — the OS download UI confirms the action. Simple, zero extra code.

options.label: Disable during download, re-enable after
options.description: Export button disables for the duration of the JS download operation (typically <100ms for JSON). Prevents double-click. Adds ~5 lines of code.

options.label: Show error state if generation fails
options.description: If the preferences JSON can’t be generated (e.g. data read error), show an inline error. Adds error handling + error UI. Only relevant if Export reads from server, not from in-memory form state.

options.label: B + C combined: disable during + error on failure
options.description: Disable Export during operation AND surface an error if generation fails. Most complete, most code.

options.label: Build it now in this PR (Recommended)
options.description: Add a code comment to the action group’s responsive styles stating DOM order must match tab order. ~3 lines. Prevents future regressions. Low effort, high permanence.

options.label: Add to TODOS.md
options.description: Defer. Risk: the next developer touching the mobile layout won’t know about the constraint and silently breaks keyboard nav.
